skill.description: Build AI-powered software with TypeSafe: small units of AI intelligence you can use like programming primitives. Its System One models, including Jev, turn natural language and application state into typed judgments and probabilities that code can combine. Use when a feature needs programmable common sense, when brainstorming what AI could make possible in an app, or when an LLM prompt-and-parse step could become a structured decision. Applications include routing, ranking, extraction, verification, and interactive experiences; these are starting points, not the limits. Read live docs and cookbooks to find useful patterns and discover new combinations.

content.user_title: Build Typed AI Decisions with TypeSafe
content.value_statement: Many application features need semantic judgments, but free-form model responses are difficult to combine reliably in code. TypeSafe helps developers design small typed judgments and compose them into routing, ranking, extraction, verification, and interactive workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guide developers in mapping application behavior to focused AI judgments.
Explain how Choice, Noul, and Score primitives represent different decision needs.
Recommend patterns for routing, selection, evidence ranking, scoring, verification, and escalation.
Show how to separate observed state, inferred state, policies, and application logic.
Advise on thresholds, uncertainty handling, reusable judgments, and representative testing.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and links; it does not implement or run a TypeSafe integration.
Current API contracts, SDK details, model limits, and version behavior require checking live documentation.
Typed output guarantees an interface, not the truth or suitability of a model judgment.
Thresholds and cookbook examples must be evaluated against the target domain and consequences.

use_cases.title: Plan semantic application features
use_cases.description: Turn a product behavior into focused judgments, typed outputs, and bounded application actions.

use_cases.title: Design evidence and review workflows
use_cases.description: Combine retrieval, relevance judgments, confidence thresholds, verification, and human escalation.

use_cases.title: Improve an existing model integration
use_cases.description: Replace broad prompt-and-parse steps with reusable primitives, explicit state, and testable composition.

prompt_templates.title: Find the right judgment
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building [feature]. It must [observable behavior]. Identify the smallest semantic judgment it needs, the relevant state, and a suitable TypeSafe primitive. Keep deterministic rules in code.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a primitive
prompt_templates.prompt: For this decision, compare Choice, Noul, and Score: [decision]. Define what each output means, when each primitive fits, and what no-match or uncertainty outcome the application needs.

prompt_templates.title: Compose a workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeSafe workflow for [goal]. Separate observed state, inferred state, policies, and execution. Identify independent questions that can run together, dependent follow-up steps, thresholds, and human escalation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed semantic workflow: [design]. Check question scope, candidate coverage, state freshness, confidence interpretation, policy handling, latency and cost, failure categories, test cases, and the boundary between model judgments and application code.

output_examples.input: A support application must route incoming messages to a known team and fill the team-specific fields.
output_examples.output: Use a routing judgment to select a team and a separate typed judgment for branch-specific arguments. Ask only the questions relevant to the selected branch, then let application code execute the handoff.

output_examples.input: A search workflow has many retrieved candidates and needs reliable context for an answer.
output_examples.output: Retrieve candidates in code, judge relevance with comparable scores, select useful evidence, and send uncertain or failing cases to verification or human review.

output_examples.input: A product team wants to replace a broad prompt that returns parsed text.
output_examples.output: Split the broad request into narrow judgments with explicit criteria, named state fields, typed outputs, a no-match result, and tests for representative cases.

best_practices: Start from the application behavior, then define the smallest judgment that supports it.
Keep rules, calculations, lookups, execution, and authorization in deterministic code.
Test judgments and resulting behavior with representative data, thresholds, and failure cases.
anti_patterns: Do not use a model judgment for exact rules, arithmetic, lookups, or permission enforcement.
Do not treat confidence as proof of correctness or reuse example thresholds without validation.
Do not send stale inferred state into actions without checking the current application state.

faq.question: What is TypeSafe used for?
faq.answer: It helps developers add focused semantic judgments to software for routing, ranking, extraction, verification, and interactive decisions.

faq.question: Which primitive should I choose?
faq.answer: Use Choice for one option, Noul for whether a condition holds, and Score for a degree along a defined dimension.

faq.question: Does this skill write integration code?
faq.answer: It provides design guidance and points to API and SDK documentation. It does not implement or execute an integration.

faq.question: How should I handle uncertainty?
faq.answer: Define thresholds using target data and consequences, include no-match outcomes, and escalate uncertain or failing cases when appropriate.

faq.question: Can TypeSafe replace application logic?
faq.answer: No. Keep deterministic rules, calculations, lookups, execution, authorization, and workflow control in code.

faq.question: What should I test?
faq.answer: Test representative inputs, state freshness, questions, candidates, outputs, composition, thresholds, service failures, and observed application behavior.
